title: Claim: sliding-window-avoids-nesting
body: Sliding window processes each element at most twice, keeping subarray problems O(n) instead of O(n^2).

title: Claim: prefix-sum-enables-constant-range-queries
body: A prefix sum array answers any subarray-sum query in O(1) after O(n) preprocessing.

title: Claim: two-pointers-solve-ksum-in-polynomial
body: Two pointers on a sorted array reduce k-sum from O(n^k) brute force to O(n^(k-1)) by solving one subproblem in linear time.

title: Claim: in-place-rotation-uses-constant-space
body: Rotating a matrix 90 degrees in place uses O(1) extra space; allocating a new matrix uses O(n^2).

title: Claim: product-except-self-without-division
body: Computing product of array except self is possible without division by combining left and right products.

title: Q2: A prefix sum array allows answering 'sum of elements from in
body:
A. O(n)
B. O(j - i)
C. O(1)

title: Q3: In 3Sum, after sorting the array, why do we use two pointers
body:
A. Two pointers are always faster than nested loops in general
B. Two pointers reduce the inner loop from O(n) to O(1), making 3Sum O(n^2) instead of O(n^3)
C. Nested loops are not allowed on sorted arrays
D. Two pointers find the exact center of the array

**B.** Fixing one element and using two pointers to find the complementary pair is O(n) per element, so O(n^2) total with sorting.

title: Q4: Why can product of array except self be computed without div
body:
A. Division would lose precision for floating-point numbers
B. Left and right products multiply to give the product of all except element i
C. All elements are guaranteed to be non-zero
D. Multiplication is always faster than division

**B.** Prefix products (left of i) and suffix products (right of i) are computed separately, then combined. This avoids division by zero and is general.

title: Q5: What is the space complexity of rotating a 90-degree matrix
body:
A. O(n)
B. O(n^2)
C. O(1)
D. O(log n)

**C.** In-place rotation using transpose and row reversal (or layer-by-layer swaps) uses only a constant number of temporary variables.

title: LeetCode 53: Maximum Subarray
body:

**Why**: At each position, choose: extend the previous subarray or start new. Tracking both maxima finds the best in O(n).

title: LeetCode 238: Product of Array Except Self
body:
**Pattern**: left products, right products, combine

**Why**: Division by zero is avoided. Left products (all before i) and right products (all after i) multiply to the result. O(n) without division.

**Python**: `two passes over the array; no division`

title: LeetCode 48: Rotate Matrix
body:
**Pattern**: transpose then reverse rows, or rotate layer by layer

**Why**: In-place rotation uses O(1) extra space by transforming indices and swapping. Allocating a new matrix would use O(n^2) space.

**Python**: `nested loops with index algebra; swap elements in place`

title: LeetCode 54: Spiral Matrix
body:
**Pattern**: traverse in layers: top row, right column, bottom row, left column

**Why**: Tracking boundaries and spiraling inward visits each element exactly once in O(n*m) with O(1) extra space.

**Python**: `four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) updated after each side`
